reason: The figures are correct, but the claim treats two papers as one. The Stocks in Play result (Sharpe 2.81, 36% alpha, 2016-2023) is Zarattini, Barbon & Aziz 2024, which appeared in the Swiss Finance Institute Research Paper Series 24-98 and so is not strictly 'self-published'. The QQQ result (33.2% vs 14.9% CAGR, zero slippage but commission charged) is a separate paper, Zarattini & Aziz April 2023 (SSRN 4416622), and the MQL5 replication tested that QQQ paper. The +0.06R out-of-sample figure is net of spread and slippage, on NQ CFDs.
found: Carlo Zarattini & Andrea Barbon & Andrew Aziz, 2024. "A Profitable Day Trading Strategy For The U.S. Equity Market," Swiss Finance Institute Research Paper Series 24-98 | In their April 2023 paper entitled "Can Day Trading Really Be Profitable? ...", Carlo Zarattini and Andrew Aziz test ... QQQ | The out-of-sample years 2021 to 2026 give +0.06 R on NQ at best
suggested_fix: A non-peer-reviewed working paper (Zarattini, Barbon & Aziz, Swiss Finance Institute RP 24-98, 2024) reports a Sharpe ratio of 2.81 and 36% annual alpha for the top-20 Stocks in Play over 2016-2023. A separate paper by Zarattini & Aziz (2023) reported 33.2% vs 14.9% CAGR for a 5-minute ORB on QQQ, charging commission but assuming no spread or slippage. An independent replication of that QQQ rule on index CFDs over 2015-2026, net of spread and slippage, found at most +0.06R per trade out of sample over 2021-2026.
